findings.comment: Proposed trees at southern boundary are planted directly at the overhead electric line with zero clearance (measured 0 feet 0 inches). Northern boundary trees are planted 0.5 feet from the overhead electric line. Utility compatibility of the proposed tree species (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) is not documented on the plans or verified against ECM Appendix F. A minimum of 15 lateral feet is required from distribution conductors. Plans must document that all trees within 15 feet of overhead distribution conductors are verified as utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F, or trees must be relocated to comply with clearance requirements.

Proposed Live Oak trees (minimum specification 100 gallon, 4-inch caliper, 16-foot height minimum) and Cedar Elm trees (100 gallon, 4-inch caliper, 16-foot height minimum) are planted along the southern boundary with zero clearance from the overhead electric line. These species have mature heights typically exceeding 40 feet per ECM Appendix F standards. Large trees (40+ feet mature height) require minimum 25 lateral feet clearance from distribution conductors. Plans do not document mature heights per Appendix F or provide required clearance distances. Trees must be relocated or documented as permitted by Austin Energy approval.

Trees are proposed 0.5 feet from the overhead electric line along the northern boundary, indicating proximity to utility poles bordering the property. A minimum of 10 lateral feet is required from utility poles. Proposed trees (particularly mitigation trees and buffer plantings along the north boundary) must be relocated to maintain 10-foot minimum clearance from poles, or applicant must provide documented Austin Energy approval for closer placement.

Large trees (40+ feet mature height) are not differentiated on the landscape plan. The plan uses symbols indicating tree function (SY=street yard, PL=parking lot, P=buffer point, M=mitigation) but does not indicate which trees are 40+ feet at maturity. This prevents verification that large trees comply with the 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors and 50-foot clearance from transmission conductors. Plans must add a designation (legend symbol or notation) to identify trees with 40+ foot mature height per ECM Appendix F.

The landscape plan does not include dimension lines or notes indicating how tree clearances from the overhead electric conductors are measured or verified. While the OHE line is shown on the plan, there are no dimension callouts demonstrating that measurements are taken from the outside conductor position rather than the pole centerline. Applicant must clarify measurement methodology by adding dimensions to show clearance distances taken from outside conductors as required by UCM § 1.10.10.4.

The landscape plan does not include dimension lines or notes verifying that tree clearances are measured from the tree trunk (planting location) rather than from projected canopy edge. While tree symbols are shown on the landscape plan, there are no dimension callouts indicating that clearance measurements originate at the tree trunk. Applicant must add dimension notes clarifying that all clearances are measured from tree trunk centerline, not canopy edge.

Although the landscape plan shows both trees and the overhead electric line symbols, clearance verification cannot be completed. Overhead electric conductors are not dimensioned on the landscape plan, and no clearance zones or restricted planting areas are indicated. Additionally, the relationship between proposed trees and overhead poles is not clear. The landscape plan must be revised to either: (1) show overhead electric infrastructure with dimensioned clearances to all proposed trees, or (2) remove all trees from within the required clearance zones and note on plan that trees comply with utility clearance requirements.

No documented written approval from Austin Energy is included with the site plan application regarding tree placements in restricted clearance zones. The Master Comment Report references Austin Energy preliminary design requirements and links to a Bluebeam review (which cannot be accessed), but no formal approval letter or variance document is submitted with the application. If trees cannot be relocated outside restricted zones, applicant must obtain and submit explicit written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the tree placements within 15 feet of distribution conductors, 25 feet for large trees, 50 feet for transmission conductors, and other applicable clearance restrictions.

Three transformer pads are shown on the electrical design plan (west, east, and south locations), and the landscape plan shows trees throughout the site. However, the landscape plan does not indicate which trees (if any) are within 10 feet of the transformer pad locations. Clearance distances from proposed trees to pad-mounted equipment are not dimensioned on either the landscape plan or electrical plan. Applicant must verify and document that no trees are proposed within 10 lateral feet of any transformer pad or pad-mounted equipment access doors, or provide documented Austin Energy approval for closer placement.

Underground electric equipment (transformer pads, pull boxes, electrical meters) locations are shown on the electrical design plan, and trees are shown on the landscape plan. However, clearance distances from proposed trees to underground equipment are not dimensioned on either plan. Pull boxes are located throughout the site at various positions, and 8 electrical meters are attached to buildings. Without dimensions showing the relationship between trees and underground equipment, compliance with the 5-foot minimum clearance for underground equipment cannot be verified. Applicant must add dimension callouts to the landscape plan showing clearances from trees to underground electric equipment, or relocate trees to maintain 5-foot clearance.

Proposed trees and underground electric equipment locations are shown on the plans, but clearance distances from trees to equipment are not dimensioned. Without documented distances, it cannot be verified which (if any) proposed trees fall within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. The landscape plan details and notes do not specify root barrier requirements or specifications. Applicant must: (1) dimension tree locations relative to underground equipment to identify any trees within 20 feet, and (2) provide root barrier details (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) for any trees within 20 feet of underground equipment, or relocate trees outside the 20-foot zone.
